item.description: Big-name prospects flipping during the early signing period has become less common over the years, but the days leading up to it tell a different story. Coaches aren't only focused on closing out the regular season; they're also making last-minute pitches to players or scheduling last-minute visits to make one final impression. The top players in the country are already committed to their respective programs, but that doesn't mean that they're locked in until they've signed on the dotted line. Now at Buford (GA), while he hasn't locked down his commitment to Texas Tech, that hasn't stopped other programs from taking their shots at him. He remained steadfast in his commitment to Texas Tech even after visits to Florida, LSU, Texas and SMU. item.title: Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished because it was ‘never built on character’
item.description: Credit: The Pivot, ESPN The final act of Aaron Rodgers’ career took a pretty shocking turn this week. The future Hall of Famer was unceremoniously benched via a social media post late Tuesday night with little explanation. In response, he showed up on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and threw his longtime coach Mike McCarthy under the bus, accusing him of falling asleep in meetings and several other shortcomings in his first year in Pittsburgh. We’ve seen great players leave the league far from their peak. Tom Brady got his last Super Bowl with the Buccaneers, but his final season in Tampa Bay was far from pretty. But nothing in that final season affected Brady’s status amongst the all-time greats. Given Rodgers’ exit was so loud, and according to many former pros , so against the unwritten rules of football life , will Rodgers see his reputation take a hit due to how this chapter ends? Ryan Clark doesn’t think so. Speaking on his show The Pivot , Clark, who has been public with his feelings about Rodgers for some time, argued that the quarterback’s legacy as a player was safe, because it was never tied to him being a good guy. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy is in no way tarnished, because his legacy was never built on character,” Clark said. “If Tom Brady says this when leaving the New England Patriots, we’re shocked. We’re surprised. Because it’s against everything he’s ever shown us. Mike McCarthy should’ve known that kissing a rattlesnake was safer than coaching Aaron Rodgers again. He’s shown many times there’s no loyalty, there’s nothing I won’t say, I won’t think about the person I’m talking about before I think about myself. Many people will say that he fell on the sword. That this was about the team. Well, you’re already out of the building. This is about you.” Clark noted that the fact that Rodgers’ former teammates were forced to answer so many questions about his departure was proof that his actions weren’t about helping the team. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that to be some sort of martyr. Aaron Rodgers did that because he got demoted and said, ‘Oh, I’m going to get you way more than you could get me.'” From there, Clark lamented what has become of his former team , arguing that he was against the hiring of McCarthy in the first place as it went against what the Steelers usually looked for in a coach. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished, because it was never built on character” Multiple things can be true at once. Aaron Rodgers can be both right & wrong. Telling the truth doesn’t preclude you from being disingenuous, & Mike McCarthy can have a winning record while operating like a bad head coach. item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 25: Cairo Santos #2 of the Chicago Bears lines up a field goal attempt in the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 25, 2021 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s edition of the Gridiron Time Machine, we’re revisiting an unlikely comeback at Arrowhead, a valuable lesson in why you should never kick to Devin Hester, and a Thanksgiving victory that came down to the final second. So hop aboard the time machine for another fantastic trip down memory lane. 1.) 1993, Bears @ Chiefs: An unlikely comeback at Arrowhead November 21, 1993 | Bears win 19-17 The Bears entered Week 12 of the 1993 season with a 4-5 record under first-year head coach Dave Wannstedt. A trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs wasn’t exactly the ideal opportunity to get back to .500. Things certainly didn’t look promising early on, as future Hall of Fame running back Marcus Allen found the end zone twice to give Kansas City a 14-0 lead in the second quarter. The Bears managed to get on the board before halftime thanks to a pair of Kevin Butler field goals from 32 and 45 yards out, cutting the deficit to eight. Chicago continued chipping away in the third quarter when Tim Worley broke loose for a 25-yard touchdown run. A blocked extra point kept the Bears from pulling within one, and a Nick Lowery field goal extended Kansas City’s lead to 17-12 heading into the fourth quarter. If you were expecting Jim Harbaugh to lead some sort of aerial assault to complete the comeback, think again. Harbaugh completed 13 of his 20 pass attempts for just 98 yards and two interceptions, finishing the afternoon with a passer rating of 37.1. He was considerably more effective with his legs, rushing for 56 yards on eight attempts. The Bears leaned heavily on their ground game, rushing for 185 yards on 43 attempts. Worley led the way with 59 yards, while Neal Anderson added another 42. With just over three minutes remaining, Anderson punched it in from one yard out to give Chicago its first lead of the afternoon. The Bears’ defense, which recorded five sacks and held Kansas City to just three second-half points, made sure that lead stuck. The Chiefs would go on to win the AFC West and reach the AFC Championship Game that season, but on this particular Sunday, the Bears had their number. Winning on the road against one of the AFC’s best teams without throwing for 100 yards? item.description: Michael Buscemi asks: Really curious about this question and answer at least in every game there is a few times a cornerback or safety drops an interception do they ever have drills for defensive backs from quarterbacks that train their hands better to catch and making deceptions it happened so often I’m just curious to see what your answer is about practicing drills to help control the ball. Ed says: Michael, these guys are at the highest level of their sport. They practice catching the ball every day — or at least every day there is a practice. There are always drills that involve catching the ball, both standing still and on the move. There is also a JUGS machine guys can use at the end of practice. Several players use it all the time. Reality is, though, game and practice conditions are much different. You practice the fundamentals of catching so that it becomes muscle memory, but you can’t mimic game speed or circumstances. John Steinbreder asks: As is the case with so many Giants fans, I am enjoying every part of the Jameis Winston Experience and the deft and very selfless ways he has been performing his duties as QB2 for the Giants. And that has me wondering: has there ever been a back-up quite like him? The thoughtful mentoring of the young signal callers. Coming in off the bench when needed to win games. And now his role as the man orchestrating the tush-push, whether as a runner or passer. Then, of course, there are the signals he actually calls, in part to try and draw the opposing team offsides and also to entertain. And his barking, “Who Let The Dogs Out” in the Commanders game still has me chortling weeks later. I am also curious as to your thoughts on Harbaugh utilizing Jameis in those situations as a way of protecting JJ from taking unnecessary shots. item.title: 3 Keys to Victory: Michigan Football at Ohio State
item.description: In the blink of an eye, Michigan’s season went from a complete and utter failure to what could be a similar story to the 2024 season. The Wolverines were 6-5 going into The Game in 2024, but the outlook on the season completely changed when it upset the No. 1 team in the country.Michigan’s 6-5 team of 2026 doesn’t have that exact same opportunity, but after beating then-No. 4 UCLA last week, it would feel similar if it capped the season off with a win over the Buckeyes. It’s the biggest game of the year, no matter the records or circumstances, as Michigan and Ohio State meet for the 122nd rendition of The Game. Here are the keys to victory for the Wolverines. Win the turnover margin Last week proved exactly why the turnover margin is so important in football, and how damaging it can be for a Michigan team that has struggled with that aspect of the game all season long. UCLA entered last Saturday with a +16 turnover margin, the best in the Big Ten and tied for second in the FBS. The Wolverines forced three turnovers and only turned it over once — the final takeaway leading to a game-altering touchdown at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Michigan is still last in the Big Ten with a -8 turnover margin, but Ohio State isn’t great either with a -3 turnover margin, tied for 14th in the conference. If it needs reminding, three of the Wolverines’ biggest wins — Week 2 against Oklahoma, Week 7 against Penn State, Week 11 against UCLA — have been the only games they won the turnover margin. One of the only faults of this Michigan defense has been its inability to force turnovers, but if last week was an indication of how The Game will go, it could be a long day for an Ohio State offense that has turned the ball over seven times in the last four games, three of which ended in losses. Keep a strong run game Freshman running back Savion Hiter had himself a game against the Bruins. For an offense that’s been struggling to find its footing all season long, especially in the run game, his performance proved something replicable. Hiter had a career-high 26 carries for 104 yards against UCLA, and it was his second consecutive game with more than 100 yards rushing. Ohio State has the 15th -best rushing defense in FBS, allowing just 100.3 yards per game. Even with the injuries and blunders of the Buckeyes’ offense, the defense has remained intact and hasn’t allowed more than 116 yards rushing to an opponent in the last four weeks, despite three of them ending in losses. If the Michigan offense can limit the negative run plays caused by blocking issues along the line, and rally behind Hiter and the run game to spark the offense, it may score just enough points to win. Continue making field goals The unsung heroes of Michigan’s win over UCLA was freshman kicker Jacob Baggett and punter Cam Brown, the latter of whom handled some difficult snaps as the holder. item.description: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up on the sideline during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix exits the Week 11 bye and enters a seven-game stretch that could define his career. With scrutiny mounting , the final two months of 2026 will not only dictate whether Penix remains the Falcons’ starter entering 2027, but could also determine whether he ever gets another shot to lead an NFL franchise. To save his job, Penix must show immediate growth in three critical areas: starting faster, surviving pocket pressure, and rediscovering his signature deep ball. Penix must fix his first-quarter freeze According to Next Gen Stats , the Falcons’ slow starts have been fueled by a 31st-ranked first-quarter EPA per play and 32nd-ranked first-quarter passing yards. Leaning on the run game would help, with Atlanta’s early-game run rate plummeting from 56 percent in Penix’s first three starts to the 24th-ranked 42 percent over the last five. But the Falcons cannot ask star running back Bijan Robinson to carry the entire offense, as Penix has to pull some weight. Per NFL.com , Penix has completed 46 percent of his throws in the first quarter while averaging just 3 yards per attempt. The Falcons have produced just six passing first downs in the first quarter in Penix’s eight starts, compared with an NFL average of 19. This keeps the team from sustaining offense, thanks to a league-low first-quarter third-down efficiency of 10 percent across Penix’s starts. This isn’t a problem unique to 2026, as Penix posted a dismal 38.8 passer rating in the first quarter during his rookie season before surging to 108.8 in his second. That leap offers hope that more time in Tommy Rees’ offense can spark a similar turnaround. But as a third-year pro, Penix’s early-game struggles are harder to excuse, and Atlanta cannot afford to wait until 2027 for competence. item.title: Rain, wind gusts up to 30 mph expected for 49ers-Seahawks showdown
item.description: Rain falls during the fourth quarter of an NFC Divisional Playoffs game between the Green Bay Packers and the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Jan. 20, 2024. (Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Sunday's pivotal matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks is set to be played in wet and windy weather . In a phone interview with SFGATE on Friday, National Weather Service meteorologist Dial Hoang said rain is expected to hit the Bay Area on Sunday morning. The rain will likely roll in from the North Bay, where it's expected to arrive shortly after sunrise, and reach Santa Clara County and the area surrounding Levi's Stadium in the late morning. Once it arrives, it won't go away for the rest of the day, he said. "We're looking at the rain continuing across the Bay Area during the game, and especially after the game," Hoang told SFGATE. "Those lingering showers may extend into Monday morning." It shouldn't be overly cold - the forecast calls for temperatures to be in the mid-60s - and shouldn't rain too heavily, with around a quarter of an inch expected. But Hoang said it will be "gusty" during Sunday's game, with wind gusts expected to be between 25 and 30 mph. "It does look like the wind is going to be a strong factor," Hoang said. It's been a wet few weeks in the Bay Area, with a Nov. 18 storm breaking rainfall records in various Bay Area cities and causing flooding in several pockets of San Francisco. The region also saw near-historic high tides last week as part of the ongoing impact of El Niño this winter. The 49ers have already made several preparations in anticipation of a rainy winter. While the players and coaches were training in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to prepare for a game in Mexico City last week, the 49ers built a rain canopy over one of their practice fields in Santa Clara. Why does this now exist at #49ers HQ? item.title: UH's 'Old Man Club' prepares for final home game after 15 combined college football seasons
item.description: Brandon Mack II's eight-year college odyssey comes to an end with UH on Saturday. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) They've heard all the jokes about their age, how long they've played college football and all the changes they've witnessed. Meet defensive linemen Brandon Mack II and Quindario Lee, card-carrying members of the University of Houston' s unofficial "Old Man Club." When the No. 18 Cougars host Baylor for Senior Night on Saturday, two of the longest-tenured players in school history will play their final home game. Eight seasons for Mack. Seven seasons for Lee. UH vs. BAYLOR: How to watch "A lot of stories with those guys, a lot of memories," said James Ross III, the Cougars' edges and defensive run-game coordinator. Both are 25 years old. Mack goes by the nickname "Unc." Lee, who is three months older, is called "Gramps." "B-Mac always reminds me I'm older," Lee said with a laugh. And you'll likely never see their type of longevity again. The NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which limits players to five seasons within a five-year window, will make it impossible to replicate careers that have combined for 15 seasons and spanned two presidential terms. "I'm just excited to see them transition into life," Ross said. He jokingly added, "We tried to find some more years. There are no more hidden years anywhere else." Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . While there is no official category, Mack and Lee are believed to be the longest-tenured players in program history. Their careers have been prolonged by an extra year of eligibility because of the COVID-19 pandemic and medical redshirts. A three-star defensive end out of high school, Mack signed with Ole Miss in 2018. He spent four seasons in Oxford, missing one with a foot injury, before transferring to UH in 2023. His first season with the Cougars ended prematurely, however, when he suffered a high-grade tear of the lat muscle on his left side in the second week of the season. He has been healthy the past three seasons, playing in 12 games in 2024 and set to play 13 games in consecutive seasons with the Cougars qualifying for a bowl. "I feel like yesterday was my first time in TDECU Stadium when we played UTSA and wore our powder blue jerseys," said Mack, who has posted 10 sacks over the past three seasons. "Then you blink and it's over. It definitely felt like it went by fast." Mack thought his college career was over last November. He began filling out information for the Cougars' Senior Night ceremony when he was told he had another year of eligibility. Lee's path has been just as winding. A three-year defensive lineman, Lee went from small-town Alabama to Fort Scott (Kan.) Community College. He transferred to Central Michigan, where he played 24 games over three seasons, before arriving at UH in 2024.

item.description: Luka Doncic accuses courtside fan of pushing him during heated wristband incident originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic had a rough Friday night in San Antonio. The Los Angeles Lakers lost 99-96 to the San Antonio Spurs , dropping their season record to 15-4. The loss also knocked Los Angeles out of the NBA Cup. Things got even worse for Doncic after the final buzzer. As he walked toward the tunnel at the Frost Bank Center, he got into an argument with a fan sitting near the walkway. Video from the arena showed Doncic tossing his wristband to a female fan. A moment later, he heard she did not want it. Doncic walked back to pick it up and the man sitting next to her returned it before shoving the Slovenian star in the back. Doncic turned around right away to confront the man. Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt and arena security quickly stepped in to separate them. After the game, Doncic spoke to reporters about what happened. He blamed the fan for starting the physical contact. "I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else," Doncic said . Stephon Castle saved Wembanyama by knocking down a 3 and giving the Spurs a six-point lead. Dissecting his underwhelming display at the charity stripe, Wembanyama told Prime Video analysts he was like O’Neal at the free-throw line. “I gotta say, I’m just like Shaq free-throw shooting-wise right now,” he said. O’Neal was one of the worst free-throw shooters in the league, and teams often fouled him in the clutch because of it. O’Neal was often benched when opponents played the foul game while trailing in close games. The Lakers legend shot 52.7% from the free-throw line. Wembanyama is much better over his career. item.title: Detroit Lions’ playoff, NFC North odds still high despite loss to Bears
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions gives a speech in the team huddle prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears was deflating and disappointing. Not so much because it was a critical game for Detroit’s playoff odds, but because the Lions were in a prime position to win and take a stranglehold on the division. But as you’ll soon see, the Lions are still in a great position to accomplish everything in front of them. Let’s look at how their playoff, NFC North, and even Super Bowl odds have shifted after their Thanksgiving loss to the Bears. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 78% (down 8%) RBSDM: 81% (down 4%) DVOA: 83.3% (down 6.3%) ESPN (FPI): 91.5% (down 5.5%) Even by the most pessimistic models, the Lions still have more than a 3-in-4 chance to make the postseason. Their loss to the Bears did not decrease their postseason odds by more than 10% across any of these four prediction models. ESPN still remains very high on the Lions, with a massive 91.5% chance to make the playoffs, but it seems like the more normal average is around 80-83%. NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 15% (down 14%) RBSDM: 20% (down 13%) DVOA: 19.3% (down 18%) ESPN (FPI): 30.6% (down 19.4%) Obviously, this loss had a bigger impact on Detroit’s chances to win the division, but the odds are not outstandingly long still. The Lions still have a 15-30% chance to win the NFC North, and that stands true because they still have three division games left. And while they’re all on the road, Detroit has proven they can go toe-to-toe with any of those teams. And the fact that Detroit has a 2-1 record in the division already gives them a nice leg up on the tiebreakers, as long as they continue to beat their divisional foes. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 4% (down 4%) RBSDM: 6% (down 6%) DVOA: 3.9% (down 6.3%) ESPN : 5% (down 6%) You can pretty much kiss the Lions’ odds for the No. 1 seed goodbye. Unless the San Francisco 49ers struggle down the stretch—and they do have tough games against the Seahawks, Giants, Rams, and Chiefs left—Detroit is not likely to finish any higher than the NFC’s No. 2 seed. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 11.0% (down 1.9%) DVOA: 7.3% (down 3.1%) Surprisingly, the Lions’ Super Bowl odds have not been impacted too much. Perhaps their strong offensive performance against a decent Bears defense has fed the models’ optimism about Detroit being able to survive a shootout game. However, their defensive performance on Thursday looms large as well.

The Red Sox have spent this offseason trying to put themselves in a position to win the AL East, though so has every other team in the best division in baseball. Jazz Chisholm Jr. signing with the Blue Jays has only added to that. While the Yankees lost a good player and a rival in Toronto landed one, the Red Sox could be affected. Or, they could hurt the Yankees even more by signing Brandon Lowe. With Chisholm gone, the Yankees have a hole at second base, and Lowe seems like one option to fill it. Ultimately, this is the type of move that helps in more ways than one, as the Red Sox would improve their own lineup and take something away from their biggest rival. Lowe fits Boston's roster as a left-handed bat with big power who can play second base. Despite a somewhat crowded infield, the Red Sox’s offense is always looking for ways to improve. He has been an elite hitter when healthy, and any contending lineup could use more of that. While the Red Sox aren’t going to make a move just to impact the Yankees, it does raise questions about how much sense this would make. The only issue Boston might consider is that Lowe was also offered the qualifying offer, similar to Jake Bauers, who it already signed. Signing Lowe would cost the Red Sox more draft picks, though his 35-home-run production would make up for it. item.title: Ian Rapoport shares what he now knows about Brock Purdy’s ankle injury
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Brock Purdy recently suffered an ankle sprain but the quarterback’s injury is not expected to be a major problem. Purdy has put himself in the NFL MVP conversation this season en route to the San Francisco 49ers going 9-1. He has a 71.0 completion rate and the joint-second-highest average yards per pass (9.0) in the NFL right now, which is only bettered by Lamar Jackson (10.0 in five games). The 49ers will have to make do without Purdy against the Seattle Seahawks this weekend but it doesn’t appear as though the QB will be sidelined for too long. Brock Purdy’s injury not considered ‘major’ Speaking on the NFL Network this week, Ian Rapoport commented on the 26-year-old’s injury and said that it is ‘not considered to be major’. He stated: “Brock Purdy has not yet practised for the San Francisco 49ers. He’s dealing with an ankle sprain. It’s not considered to be major, but if a starting quarterback doesn’t practise at all, you don’t think he has a chance to play.” WebMD have previously reported that Grade 1 ankle sprains take around 1-3 weeks to recover from. Grade 2 could take 4-6 weeks and a Grade 3 could rule an NFL player out for ‘several months’. However, based on Rapoport’s comments saying Purdy’s issue is not ‘major’, it looks as though his problem would be classified in the Grade 1 category. After this week’s game with the Seahawks, the 49ers are next in action on December 6 against the New York Giants. They will then play the Los Angeles Rams on December 13 before clashing with the Los Angeles Chargers on December 17. Purdy could miss all three of those games if his injury recovery time is on the higher end of a Grade 1 sprain, but there is also a chance he could be back in a week’s time to face the Giants. item.title: 'I am not prepared': Rohit Sharma reveals how he agreed to return as Mumbai Indians captain
item.description: NEW DELHI: Veteran batter Rohit Sharma is back in charge of Mumbai Indians after a three-year hiatus, but the five-time IPL-winning captain says his return was not driven by a desire to reclaim the leadership role. It was the feeling that the franchise needed direction after a difficult few seasons. Rohit was on Friday reinstated as Mumbai Indians captain ahead of the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League. He will succeed Hardik Pandya, who has joined Punjab Kings in a trade involving pacer Arshdeep Singh. Rohit, who led Mumbai to five IPL titles, admitted that he was initially unsure about taking up the responsibility again. The decision came after discussions with the franchise management and some thought about the team's future. "My honest thought initially was, I am not prepared for this right now. I have to go back and think about it kyunki kaafi kuch ho chuka tha. Toh I don't know if I was in that frame of mind to do it or not," Rohit said in an interview. However, he eventually felt that the team needed someone to take it forward. "But then andar se feeling aisa aaya ki yaar I am not saying that this team needs me as a leader, but this team needs a direction right now. And whatever that direction is, if it is me, I am more than happy to drive this team forward," he added. 'That's not MI' Rohit's decision came against the backdrop of a disappointing run for Mumbai Indians. After winning the IPL in 2020, the franchise struggled to reproduce its earlier success. Mumbai finished fifth in 2021 and 10th in 2022 under Rohit. They reached Qualifier 2 in 2023 before the management decided to make a change in leadership, with Pandya replacing Rohit. The change did not bring the desired results either. Mumbai finished 10th in 2024, reached Qualifier 2 in 2025 and ended the 2026 season in ninth place. Rohit said the team's struggles had frustrated several players and made him reflect on how Mumbai could return to its old standards. "Look, I mean as soon as we finished the IPL, we had a very disappointing season and I was like not just me but many other players were quite frustrated with how we were playing," he said. "Main ghar gaya, I thought about it ki yaar it's not the team that used to be once upon a time. We need to get back to that. How can we do that? It happens to any team when you have seen such a high, there is bound to be a low." The 39-year-old was particularly concerned that Mumbai were not competing at the level expected of a franchise that had enjoyed so much success. "Disappointment qualification ka nahi hai. item.title: 'An embarrassing figure!' - Roberto Mancini takes aim at Serie A clubs as Italy crisis forces drastic youth gamble
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Roberto Mancini has blasted Serie A's "embarrassing" lack of domestic talent after being forced to call up inexperienced teenagers for Italy's Nations League campaign. With the national side missing out on the quarter-finals, the head coach admitted he must take bold risks to rebuild the squad. Mancini turns to youth in Nations League Mancini has revealed that a shortage of domestic players in Serie A left him little option but to hand international call-ups to youngsters with minimal top-flight experience. Speaking in an interview with Corriere dello Sport , the Italy coach addressed his recent squad selections. Ahead of this month's Nations League fixtures, Mancini drafted several teenagers into the national team camp, including youth players Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani. The move came during a mixed international window for Italy, who defeated France before a 4-1 loss to Belgium ended their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. 'Embarrassing' Serie A numbers force change At the heart of Mancini's frustration is the shrinking pool of eligible players competing regularly in Italy's top division. With domestic representation dropping sharply, the coach believes he must look beyond established club regulars to keep the national side competitive. "I was forced to (call up young players), given that the proportion of Italian players in Serie A has fallen to 30%. It's an embarrassing figure," Mancini admitted. "I have no choice but to seek out young players with potential who are capable of developing." Club indifference and a 20-year problem Italy's current struggles come against a sobering recent backdrop. Despite being four-time world champions, the national side have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups. Against Belgium, Mancini showed his willingness to trust emerging talent by handing an international debut to 20-year-old striker Alphadjo Cisse, who has scored ten goals for AC Milan this season. Mancini insists the structural issue is nothing new and expects no favours from domestic teams. "I have to take risks by fielding them in important matches," he said. "The clubs have no interest in the national team, which has to find its own solutions. There's no point in complaining about the situation that has existed for at least 20 years, we simply have to scout for players and give them experience, even if it means risking a few defeats." A long-term gamble for Italy's future With their Nations League campaign over at the group stage, Italy now face a defining period of transition. The national team will continue scouting emerging prospects and fast-tracking them into senior international football. Although this approach carries the risk of short-term setbacks, Italy clearly hopes that this early experience will ultimately pay off on the biggest stage.

item.title: Chad Johnson names the NFL team Aaron Rodgers could join immediately
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images What happens next to Aaron Rodgers is the question on the lips of a lot of people around the NFL, following what has certainly been a dramatic week. The 42-year-old quarterback will have likely watched his former team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, comfortably beat the Denver Broncos on Friday. It was the first game that Mike McCarthy’s team has played since Rodgers was released. A lot of damage has now been done to Rodgers’ reputation, which was already far from flawless, with teams across the league left considering whether bringing in the opinionated free agent quarterback is actually worth the risk. The Broncos need a much higher level from their quarterback if they are going to make any waves in the postseason. Whether Rodgers would offer that is an entirely different question, with the veteran having a lot more than just football on his mind right now after his Steelers saga. item.title: ‘They took this public’: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after locker room remarks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers has insisted that when his football career is over, he’ll go quietly into the background. However, after an ugly exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers, including a benching, a tell-all call on The Pat McAfee Show, and his subsequent release, Rodgers is making sure his voice is heard and that he has a say in the narrative. During Thursday’s call of the Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles game, Fox analyst and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady was critical of Aaron Rodgers calling into McAfee’s show to air out his grievances. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players,” Brady said. “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates. You’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.” “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place” Tom Brady takes issue with how Aaron Rodgers handled his Steelers benching on Wednesday https://t.co/gRRpgcKo41 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 27, 2026 Rodgers’ former team hosted the Denver Broncos on Friday, and Rodgers made sure that he got the final word as far as “sanctity” goes. This time, Rodgers sent a text to Prime Video play-by-play man Al Michaels, who was on the call for Friday’s game. “Been the only story in town, of course, the Aaron Rodgers saga,” Michaels said during his broadcast of the Steelers’ 27-5 win over Denver. “Earlier today, I heard from Aaron, who said, he said, ‘A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room.’ “He said, ‘The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.’ He then also said, ‘They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leak at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.” For his part, even as Rodgers does his best to control the narrative, Michaels feels that the quarterback’s legacy has taken a hit. If this is truly it for Rodgers, it was an ugly end to what was an extraordinary career. item.title: Matt Coronato’s Return to New York Brings Back Memories of a Rare Feat in Flames History
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Coronato scored his seventh goal of the season Friday against the New Jersey Devils, giving the Calgary Flames forward goals in back-to-back games heading into Saturday’s matchup against the New York Rangers. The Long Island native has a little more reason to look forward to playing at Madison Square Garden than most of his teammates, though. The last time Coronato made his way through all three NHL arenas in the New York area on the same road trip, he accomplished something only Jarome Iginla had done in Flames history. Coronato joined Iginla in the Flames’ record books The Flames were fighting for a playoff spot in March 2025 when they visited the Rangers, Devils and New York Islanders in a span of five days. Coronato entered the trip with 16 goals on the season and left with 20, helping the Flames collect all six available points. As FlamesNation’s Ryan Pike pointed out at the time , Coronato became just the second player in franchise history to score in all three New York-area arenas on the same road trip. Iginla was the first to do it in December 1999. Part of what makes the feat so rare is that Calgary had only played all three teams on the same road trip seven times since the Devils relocated to New Jersey in 1982. Coronato scored the game-winning goal on the power play against the Rangers on March 18, beating Igor Shesterkin from the slot. Two nights later, an attempted pass to Nazem Kadri deflected off Dawson Mercer’s stick and beat former Flames goaltender Jacob Markstrom. Coronato saved his best performance for the team he grew up cheering for, scoring twice against the Islanders on March 22. He opened the scoring just 36 seconds into the game before scoring his 20th goal of the season in the second period. The four goals accounted for 20% of Coronato’s production through that point in the season, and he did it in his first NHL appearances in all three buildings. While reaching the 20-goal mark for the first time in his career would’ve been special regardless of where it happened, doing it against his childhood team with family in the area made for a pretty memorable week. Coronato is finding his scoring touch again Coronato’s goal against New Jersey on Friday came after some good work below the goal line by Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev, the latter of whom was one of two players Calgary received in the Tyler Toffoli trade . Coronato found some open ice in the slot and beat Jake Allen to tie the game at 2-2. The Flames forward is up to seven goals and 12 assists through Calgary’s first 27 games of the season. He’s been more productive as a playmaker than a goal scorer to this point, but Calgary invested $45.5 million in Coronato over seven years in large part because of his ability to put the puck in the net. item.description: SEC commissioner Greg Sankey talks during a press conference before a celebration for OU joining the Southeastern Conference in Norman, Okla., Monday, July 1, 2024. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey is facing another serious development in his escalating dispute with LSU. However, this time, the controversy extends beyond his role as the conference’s commissioner. A newly amended lawsuit has placed Sankey himself at the center of a legal fight involving an LSU basketball player, with allegations that could carry personal financial consequences. The development comes just days before SEC university presidents and chancellors are scheduled to consider LSU’s future in the conference. Greg Sankey Personally Named in Amended Lawsuit Former LSU basketball player RJ Luis Jr. filed an amended lawsuit Wednesday, Nov. 25, naming Sankey as a defendant in both his official and personal capacities. According to reporting from Reuters and ESPN, Luis is seeking unspecified financial damages related to the SEC’s handling of his eligibility dispute. The filing also requests a jury trial. Luis’ attorneys allege that Sankey and the conference deliberately interfered with his opportunity to compete for LSU. They further contend that the commissioner acted with malice toward their client. Those claims remain allegations and have not been established in court. Nevertheless, the decision to name Sankey personally represents a significant escalation in the dispute. Lawsuit Alleges SEC Commissioner Threatened LSU The controversy centers on LSU’s decision to allow Luis to play basketball despite the SEC’s objections to his eligibility. Luis previously signed professional basketball contracts after his time at St. John’s. The SEC maintains eligibility standards restricting participation by athletes with certain professional experience. However, Luis obtained a Louisiana court injunction protecting his ability to compete without conference penalties. He subsequently made his LSU debut against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. Luis recorded 11 points and nine rebounds in 15 minutes. According to the amended lawsuit, Sankey communicated to LSU President Wade Rousse that the university could lose its SEC membership if Luis appeared in another game. The alleged communication occurred Nov. 19, one day after Luis’ debut. Rousse subsequently instructed LSU basketball coach Will Wade not to play Luis again. Luis’ attorneys argue that the conference’s actions effectively prevented their client from continuing his college basketball career. LSU Player Seeks Financial Damages The amended filing outlines several categories of alleged financial and personal harm. item.title: Nations Championship finals weekend results, fixtures and hemisphere shield score
item.description: The inaugural Nations Championship has reached its climax with the finals weekend seeing six top-class international rugby matches across an action-packed three days at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham , with either South Africa or France set to be crowned the first-ever winner on Sunday evening The new competition has pitted the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows, with all 12 teams having had their seedings for this finals weekend determined by those results. The Springboks topped the southern hemisphere table, while France did likewise in the northern hemisphere standings, meaning those two heavyweights will clash for the title at 4.40pm GMT on Sunday – in a rematch of their incredible battle in Paris, narrowly won by Les Bleus , earlier this month – with the victors lifting the Nations Championship trophy. Before that, there will be five other matches across three days with each country facing their equivalent finisher from the group stage – including tantalising match-ups such as England against the All Blacks and Scotland v Argentina . Meanwhile the two hemispheres will also battle for the Hemisphere Shield in a ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system across the weekend. Here’s everything you need to know about finals weekend: Finals weekend results and fixtures - Allianz Stadium, Twickenham FRIDAY 27 NOVEMBER 6th vs 6th: Italy 23-21 Fiji 3rd vs 3rd: Ireland 38-14 Australia SATURDAY 28 NOVEMBER 5th vs 5th (1.10pm): Wales vs Japan 2nd vs 2nd (4.40pm): England vs New Zealand SUNDAY 29 NOVEMBER 4th vs 4th (1.10pm): Scotland vs Argentina 1st vs 1st – Nations Championship final (4.40pm): France vs South Africa What is the Hemisphere Shield? In addition to the Nations Championship itself, the Hemisphere Shield is also on offer as the northern hemisphere and southern hemisphere go head to head across the weekend. A ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system will decide its fate with each victory in the matches featuring the second- to sixth-place finishers worth one point and victory in the Nations Championship final itself worth two points – meaning seven points are on offer and the first hemisphere to rack up four points will claim the Hemisphere Shield. In the event of a draw in the 6th vs 6th, 5th vs 5th, 4th vs 4th, 3rd vs 3rd or 2nd vs 2nd matches, the game will go to 10 minutes of golden point extra time (with the first team to score being declared the winners) and if neither side scores, each team will receive half a point towards the Hemisphere Shield. The final cannot end in a draw, so if the scores are still level after golden point extra time, then a place-kicking contest will occur to decide the champion. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama enters Saturday’s Iron Bowl with one championship opportunity already gone. However, Auburn has an opportunity to deliver an even more painful blow to the Crimson Tide. The annual rivalry returns to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, with Alabama attempting to protect its College Football Playoff position. Meanwhile, Auburn has an opportunity to turn an otherwise disappointing season into an unforgettable one. And the Tigers could accomplish that by ruining their biggest rival’s postseason outlook. Alabama Already Received Bad News Before Iron Bowl Alabama entered rivalry weekend with an opportunity to reach the SEC Championship Game. However, the Crimson Tide needed help from other conference opponents. Texas’ victory over Texas A&M on Friday eliminated Alabama from the conference championship race. The Longhorns will face Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Consequently, Alabama must now pursue a national championship without another opportunity to improve its résumé in the SEC title game. That makes Saturday’s rivalry matchup especially important. A victory would allow Alabama to finish the regular season at 10-2. However, a loss would leave the Crimson Tide at 9-3 and introduce another layer of uncertainty into the playoff selection process. Auburn Could Deliver Alabama’s Worst-Case Scenario Auburn enters Saturday’s game at 7-4 following three consecutive victories. The Tigers most recently defeated Samford 59-17, producing one of their strongest offensive performances of the season. However, Saturday presents a considerably more difficult challenge. Alabama has won three consecutive games, outscoring those opponents by a combined 99-19. The Crimson Tide also enters the weekend ranked among the nation’s top College Football Playoff contenders. Nevertheless, the Iron Bowl has repeatedly demonstrated that records and expectations do not always determine the outcome. An Auburn victory would represent a major upset. More importantly, it would hand Alabama a third loss just before the playoff selection committee begins making its final decisions. Could Alabama Miss the College Football Playoff? Alabama currently holds a strong position in the playoff race. However, a third defeat could create significant uncertainty surrounding its postseason destination. The selection committee considers factors including overall record, strength of schedule, head-to-head results and performance against common opponents. item.title: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision
item.description: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics decided to make a move that seemed to be one of the more impressive of the offseason when they signed Mitchell Robinson, the former Knicks NBA champion. To say that Robinson's time in Boston has gone as planned would be wrong, as he's been very below average, to say the least. The Celtics, however, are very fortunate that some other players have stepped up in his struggles, including Neemias Queta. Queta, who hasn't always been a player who the Celtics can count on, has been with Boston since 2023-2024. Before the 2025-26 season, he had started in only six games in his entire career. Last year he started in 75, and this year he started in 12 of the 17 he's played. Queta is playing better than ever, putting up career highs in multiple statistics, including 10.4 points per game. But it also raises the question of what the Celtics could do with Robinson. If there is any possibility of moving on from Robinson, somebody like Queta playing at this level definitely helps. If the Celtics hadn't gotten this type of production out of the big man, they would find themselves in one of the more difficult positions in the NBA because of it. Instead, the Celtics now have a player they can trade in a couple of weeks and should still get a somewhat decent package. item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to Aaron Rodgers in emphatic fashion. item.description: The peeing-dog celebration made another Egg Bowl appearance Friday in Oxford, Mississippi, late in the Ole Miss Rebels’ 41-17 win over the Mississippi State Bulldogs. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
